onboarding.title: WELCOME TO THE PIDOTS CONSOLE
onboarding.subtitle: Practical guide to navigate the terminal, files, and bench resources.
onboarding.toast_completed: Operational tour completed. The terminal is ready for your instructions.

step1.title: SIDEBAR AND SPACES LIBRARY
step1.what: Here live your files, agents, and routines saved in local SQLite. Each Space is a living document you edit together with bots.
step1.how: Click rail icons to browse context panes or select a Space to load code directly onto the workbench canvas.
step1.tip: Shortcuts: <kbd>Alt+1</kbd> to <kbd>Alt+5</kbd> switch panes; <kbd>Ctrl+B</kbd> hides the sidebar to reclaim screen space.

step2.title: TELETYPE: AGENT COMMAND TERMINAL
step2.what: The main feed operates like a continuous teletype ribbon. All responses, bot thoughts, and tool outputs print here in real time.
step2.how: Type your prompt directly, use <kbd>@name</kbd> to speak with a specific bot, or <kbd>/</kbd> to open the 35 quick commands.
step2.tip: <kbd>Enter</kbd> sends instructions, <kbd>Shift+Enter</kbd> creates line breaks, and <kbd>Ctrl+L</kbd> clears the paper ribbon without wiping database logs.

step3.title: DOT'S COMPUTER: LINUX BWRAP SANDBOX
step3.what: Each agent runs inside an isolated Linux sandbox via Bubblewrap (/workspace). The bot compiles, edits, and tests code without touching host files.
step3.how: Inspect the active workspace directory at the top. Click <kbd>[Observation Mode]</kbd> to open an interactive terminal and assume control.
step3.tip: Native ARM64 process with minimal privileges: no Docker-in-Docker overhead and zero wasted memory.

step4.title: LIVE CANVAS: YOUR WORKING WORKBENCH
step4.what: Where code and documents take shape live. The workbench is divided into 4 tabs: Artifact (code & diffs), CoAgents (bot state), Terminal, and HITL Governance.
step4.how: Switch tabs to inspect execution plans, view raw logs, and approve risky commands held in the security queue.
step4.tip: <kbd>Alt+I</kbd> focuses the active artifact, <kbd>Alt+H</kbd> opens the security queue, and <kbd>Ctrl+S</kbd> saves revisions to SQLite.

step5.title: ARM64 TELEMETRY & SETTINGS
step5.what: Monitor silicon health in real time: SoC board temperature, physical RAM usage, and SQLite state. Swap AI models and API keys on-the-fly without restarting.
step5.how: Click the telemetry footer or press <kbd>Alt+5</kbd> to open settings and verify connectivity with your AI provider.
step5.tip: Need details on a route or tool? Press <kbd>F1</kbd> to display the full Technical Manual.

onboarding.step1_desc: piDots turns your edge device into a smart workstation. Lightweight async Python monolith running multiple specialists using under 70 MB RAM.
onboarding.step2_desc: Speak directly to coworkers by typing @coder for code, @architect for docs, and @auditor for command review. The supervisor coordinates teamwork.
onboarding.step3_desc: Files, code diffs, and diagrams appear in the right-side canvas without cluttering chat. Inspect diffs and restore revisions at any time.
onboarding.step4_desc: High-risk operational commands (such as deleting files or modifying system configs) are paused immediately. You review parameters before granting execution.
onboarding.step5_desc: Fast navigation: F1 opens the manual, Alt+I inspects artifacts, Ctrl+L clears the screen. Install as PWA on mobile or desktop for full-screen mode.

landing.hero_eyebrow: ARM64 CORTEX-A72 · 6.2W USB-C · < 70MB RAM RSS · OPEN SOURCE MIT
landing.hero_title_html: Autonomous AI agents on your own hardware.
landing.hero_desc: Run a persistent team of AI coworkers on Raspberry Pi 4B using less than 70 MB RAM and 6.2 Watts. Durable SQLite WAL memory, sub-15ms Bubblewrap isolation, and real-time human approval for risky commands without recurring cloud invoices.
landing.sec3_title: Auditable hardware metrics captured in real runtime
landing.sec3_lead: We replaced subjective adjectives with empirical figures pulled straight from the Linux ARM64 kernel under continuous load.
landing.sec4_title: Autonomous AI Coworker team with distinct roles
landing.sec4_lead: Each Dot runs as a dedicated specialist with its own persona, tuned system prompt, and granular execution boundaries.
landing.sec5_title: Built for physical silicon, not infinite cloud resources
landing.sec5_lead: While enterprise frameworks rely on multiple heavy containers and hidden browsers, piDots is tuned to run comfortably within 4GB SBC nodes.
landing.sec6_title: What changes when you migrate to sovereign local hardware
landing.sec6_lead: See how piDots differs from traditional cloud setups and heavy agent frameworks that treat AI as high-cost black boxes.
landing.sec7_title: Execution Arena: Bench Testing in Real Time
landing.sec7_lead: Simulate the guardrails that block unauthorized commands, see agents reviewing code as a team, and check out automatic self-healing for failing scripts.
landing.sec8_title: Calculate how fast physical hardware pays for itself versus cloud fees
landing.sec8_lead: Adjust sliders to project real cumulative savings when swapping costly virtual cloud instances for a local physical node.
landing.sec9_title: Frequently asked questions about hardware, boundaries, and safety
landing.sec9_lead: Straightforward technical answers covering memory, flash storage preservation, governance, and model connectivity.
landing.sec10_title: Put your AI team to work in 45 seconds
landing.sec10_lead: No extra manual setup. A single Docker Compose command spins up all services with telemetry and governance ready to go.
